name_note: GTDB g__Actinomyces is narrower than the classical genus: species once called Actinomyces now sit in Schaalia, Winkia, Gleimia, Pauljensenia or Bowdeniella.

sentences.text: Actinomyces species are Gram-positive, non-spore-forming rods that live as commensals of the human mouth, gut, female genital tract and skin.
In the mouth they belong to the dental biofilm, and oral species are among those most often recovered from people.
Plaque Actinomyces act as partners for coaggregation on the tooth surface; Porphyromonas gingivalis fimbriae mediate adhesion to Actinomyces viscosus.
The classical genus has been split, with several former Actinomyces species moved to Bowdeniella, Gleimia, Pauljensenia, Schaalia and Winkia.
